package_info.package_name: Azure API Management (APIM) legacy API endpoints
package_info.package_manager: Azure Cloud Platform (not a traditional package manager, but a managed service)
package_info.package_versions: All versions with legacy API endpoints enabled (pre-June 2024 deployments, especially those with legacy ARM API access)
package_info.why_malicious: The legacy API endpoints in Azure API Management expose a critical privilege escalation vulnerability: users with only Reader permissions can access deprecated endpoints to retrieve administrative SSO tokens. This bypasses intended access controls, allowing attackers to gain full administrative control, access sensitive data, and modify or deploy APIs. The flaw enables unauthorized privilege escalation and total compromise of the APIM service.

execution_context.trigger: API call initiated by attacker at runtime
execution_context.file_location: Legacy Azure Resource Manager (ARM) API endpoint: /providers/Microsoft.ApiManagement/service/{serviceName}/listSecrets

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the attacker issues a GET request to the deprecated /listSecrets ARM API endpoint using only Reader permissions, which results in the retrieval of an SSO token with full administrative privileges, enabling privilege escalation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This API call is suspicious because it allows a user with only Reader permissions to access a deprecated endpoint and retrieve an administrative SSO token, which should be restricted to higher-privilege roles.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Under normal circumstances, Reader permissions should not grant access to secrets or administrative tokens. The actual behavior violates least privilege principles by enabling privilege escalation from Reader to Admin.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate use case would involve an administrator retrieving secrets for operational needs via supported endpoints, never a Reader role or through deprecated endpoints.
key_indicators: Use of old API version parameter (e.g., api-version=2016-10-10)
Access to secrets or SSO tokens by accounts with Reader permissions
Audit log entries showing Reader role accessing privileged endpoints

execution_context.trigger: API call after obtaining SSO token (runtime, attacker-initiated)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After obtaining the admin SSO token, the attacker authenticates API requests to the APIM Management API, performing administrative actions such as deploying new APIs, modifying existing APIs, and accessing all sensitive configuration data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior is suspicious because it leverages an SSO token obtained through privilege escalation to perform high-impact administrative actions, which should only be possible for legitimate admin users.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal API usage requires proper admin authentication for sensitive operations. Here, a Reader escalates to admin and performs unauthorized administrative actions, violating access control policies.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: A legitimate admin would use an SSO token to manage APIs, but a Reader role should never be able to obtain or use such a token for these actions.
key_indicators: Use of SSO tokens obtained via deprecated endpoints
Administrative API actions performed by accounts with no prior admin privileges
Audit logs showing privilege escalation followed by sensitive operations

attack_chain.action: Attacker with Reader permissions calls a deprecated ARM API endpoint (/listSecrets) to retrieve an administrative SSO token.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker obtains an admin-level SSO token, enabling privilege escalation.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uses the admin SSO token to authenticate against the APIM Management API and perform unauthorized administrative actions, such as deploying or modifying APIs and accessing secrets.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of the APIM service and access to all sensitive data and configuration.

behavioral_signatures: API calls to deprecated ARM endpoints (e.g., /listSecrets) by users with Reader permissions
Retrieval of SSO tokens or secrets by non-admin accounts
Subsequent administrative API actions (deployments, modifications, secret access) from accounts previously limited to Reader role
Audit log correlation of privilege escalation followed by sensitive operations
file_indicators: No direct file indicators (cloud API abuse), but Azure audit logs showing access to /listSecrets or similar deprecated endpoints by Reader accounts
network_indicators: Unusual API calls to management.azure.com with old API versions (e.g., api-version=2016-10-10)
Burst of administrative API calls from accounts with no prior admin activity
Sequence of network requests: deprecated endpoint access followed by privileged API operations
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Azure audit logs for API calls to deprecated endpoints such as /listSecrets by users with Reader permissions. Flag any retrieval of SSO tokens or secrets by non-admin accounts. Correlate subsequent administrative actions (API deployments, modifications, or secret access) performed by accounts that recently escalated privileges via legacy endpoints. Alert on use of old API versions in management API calls and on sequences where privilege escalation is followed by sensitive operations.
